newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-SORENSTAM WINS LPGA TOURNAMENT OF CHAMPIONS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SORENSTAM WINS LPGA TOURNAMENT OF CHAMPIONS.

text.p: Annika Sorenstam fired a 6-under-par 66 on Sunday to begin the 1997 season with a four-stroke victory over Australia's Karrie Webb at the LPGA Tournament of Champions.
Sorenstam, who began the final round tied with Webb, finished at 16-under 272 to break the tournament record of 275 set last year by fellow Swede Liselotte Neumann.
Sorenstam earned $115,000 for the win, her sixth on the LPGA Tour, including back-to-back U.S. Women's Open titles.
Sorenstam got off to a quick start with a pair of birdies. She gave back a stroke with a bogey on three, but birdied the fourth hole by draining a 14-foot putt.
She three-putted on six for a bogey, but birdied eight to get back to 2-under heading into the back nine, where she picked up four more birdies, including three in a row beginning on 15.
"I'm amazed at how I played today," said Sorenstam. "I feel great, it's been a great week. I never putted this well.
"Karrie hit it closer on a lot of holes, but I would make the putt," Sorenstam said. "She must have been getting tired of that, I would be."
Webb, who became the first rookie golfer to eclipse $1 million in earnings last year, carded a 2-under 70 to finish second here for the second year in a row.
The 22-year-old Australian won four tournaments in 1996 to earn LPGA Rookie of the Year honours.
Webb trailed by just one stroke after the front nine. But her bogey on 14 offset a birdie on 12 and Sorenstam's three consecutive birdies sealed the win.
"It was pretty depressing to watch Annika hole all these putts," Webb said.
"No one expected me to finish second here last year, especially me," she added. "I'm off to a good start again this year, so I'm happy with second. I had a good time and played well, so I'm happy."
Barb Mucha, who began the day one shot off the lead, carded a 2-under 70 to finish third with an 11-under 277, while Michelle McGann and Nancy Lopez tied for fourth at 3-under 285.
The Tournament of Champions field was comprised of the 37 players who won tournaments in 1995 and 1996.
